problems.source_says: All five outcomes are assigned after_ai, but the saved paper establishes only that the laboratory session followed the essay assignments by one week. It describes supplying ChatGPT accounts to the treatment group and an interest in spillover effects; it does not explicitly say access was removed, blocked, or prohibited while participants produced the laboratory strategies and slogans. Codebook section 1 requires AI to have been removed, not merely a later session or an intended spillover question. The null availability fields are appropriately cautious, but the definite question assignments are unsupported; question should remain null pending the laboratory protocol.
problems.quote: One week after all assignments were submitted, the two groups were asked to take part in a lab experiment.
problems.locator: PDF p. 9, Methods, lines 187-198; laboratory procedure on PDF pp. 10-11, lines 204-239; theoretical intention on PDF p. 5, lines 92-95; creativity-codebook.md section 1, question table and assignment rule.

problems.source_says: The number 265 is explicitly the corpus of unique advertising messages, not an explicitly reported number of observations in the statistical analysis. Four coders rated the messages, but neither the results text nor Figure 3 states how their ratings were aggregated or whether the Mann-Whitney analysis used messages, individual ratings, or participant aggregates. Codebook sections 6-7 define unit and n_units in terms of analysis observations. With unit correctly left null, n_units also needs to remain null; retain 265 as the descriptive corpus size in measure_detail and reported.
problems.quote: This task culminated in 265 unique messages (as some participants chose not to change their messages at some rounds).
problems.locator: PDF p. 14, Results, lines 295-300; PDF p. 25, Figure 3; creativity-codebook.md section 6, Unit, and section 7, Signs and counts.

problems.source_says: Table 2 prints -0.719** with (0.326) and -0.604* with (0.328), but neither the table nor the associated results passage identifies the parenthesized quantities explicitly as standard errors. The table note states clustering by Subject ID and significance thresholds only. The numerical transcription is correct, and the form's reported text correctly acknowledges the missing label, but its definite regression_coefficient_se tag asserts an unconfirmed interpretation. Retain the printed quantities without treating their identity as standard errors as verified.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 correctly reports 265 unique messages, four coders, and Mann-Whitney U p-value > 0.05. Those statements establish the corpus and the reported nonsignificant result, not the test's observation count.

summary: Criterion 3 holds because external annotators rated participants' advertising messages for creativity. The coding is refuted by unsupported after_ai assignments, an unverified slogan-analysis observation count, and an unconfirmed standard-error label; the transcribed outcome statistics match the saved PDF.
